1 --- 2 title: after 3 description: API Reference for the after function. 4 --- 5 6 `after` allows you to schedule work to be executed after a response (or prerender) is finished. This is useful for tasks and other side effects that should not block the response, such as logging and analytics. 7 8 It can be used in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata)), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), and [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy). 9 10 The function accepts a callback that will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished: 11 12 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 13 import { after } from 'next/server' 14 // Custom logging function 15 import { log } from '@/app/utils' 16 17 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 18 after(() => { 19 // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user 20 log() 21 }) 22 return <>{children} 23 } 24 ``` 25 26 ```jsx filename="app/layout.jsx" switcher 27 import { after } from 'next/server' 28 // Custom logging function 29 import { log } from '@/app/utils' 30 31 export default function Layout({ children }) { 32 after(() => { 33 // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user 34 log() 35 }) 36 return <>{children} 37 } 38 ``` 39 40 > **Good to know:** `after` is not a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) and calling it does not cause a route to become dynamic. If it's used within a static page, the callback will execute at build time, or whenever a page is revalidated. 41 42 ## Reference 43 44 ### Parameters 45 46 - A callback function which will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished. 47 48 ### Duration 49 50 `after` will run for the platform's default or configured max duration of your route. If your platform supports it, you can configure the timeout limit using the [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration) route segment config. 51 52 ## Good to know 53 54 - `after` will be executed even if the response didn't complete successfully. Including when an error is thrown or when `notFound` or `redirect` is called. 55 - You can use React `cache` to deduplicate functions called inside `after`. 56 - `after` can be nested inside other `after` calls, for example, you can create utility functions that wrap `after` calls to add additional functionality. 57 58 ## Examples 59 60 ### With request APIs 61 62 Whether you can use request APIs like [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) inside `after` depends on where `after` is called from. 63 64 #### In Route Handlers and Server Functions 65 66 You can call `cookies` and `headers` directly inside the `after` callback when used in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) and [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). This is useful for logging activity after a mutation or API request. For example: 67 68 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" highlight={2,10-16} switcher 69 import { after } from 'next/server' 70 import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers' 71 import { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils' 72 73 export async function POST(request: Request) { 74 // Perform mutation 75 // ... 76 77 // Log user activity for analytics 78 after(async () => { 79 const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown' 80 const sessionCookie = 81 (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous' 82 83 logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent }) 84 }) 85 86 return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), { 87 status: 200, 88 headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, 89 }) 90 } 91 ``` 92 93 ```js filename="app/api/route.js" highlight={2,10-16} switcher 94 import { after } from 'next/server' 95 import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers' 96 import { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils' 97 98 export async function POST(request) { 99 // Perform mutation 100 // ... 101 102 // Log user activity for analytics 103 after(async () => { 104 const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown' 105 const sessionCookie = 106 (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous' 107 108 logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent }) 109 }) 110 111 return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), { 112 status: 200, 113 headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, 114 }) 115 } 116 ``` 117 118 #### In Server Components (pages and layouts) 119 120 [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including pages, layouts, and `generateMetadata`) **cannot** use `cookies`, `headers`, or other Request-time APIs inside `after`. 248 Reference: supporting `after` for serverless platforms 249 250 Using `after` in a serverless context requires waiting for asynchronous tasks to finish after the response has been sent. In Next.js and Vercel, this is achieved using a primitive called `waitUntil(promise)`, which extends the lifetime of a serverless invocation until all promises passed to [`waitUntil`](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/functions-api-reference#waituntil) have settled. 251 252 If you want your users to be able to run `after`, you will have to provide your implementation of `waitUntil` that behaves in an analogous way. 253 254 When `after` is called, Next.js will access `waitUntil` like this: 255 256 ```jsx 257 const RequestContext = globalThis[Symbol.for('@next/request-context')] 258 const contextValue = RequestContext?.get() 259 const waitUntil = contextValue?.waitUntil 260 ``` 261 262 Which means that `globalThis[Symbol.for('@next/request-context')]` is expected to contain an object like this: 263 264 ```tsx 265 type NextRequestContext = { 266 get(): NextRequestContextValue | undefined 267 } 268 269 type NextRequestContextValue = { 270 waitUntil?: (promise: Promise) => void 271 } 272 ``` 273 274 Here is an example of the implementation. 275 276 ```tsx 277 import { AsyncLocalStorage } from 'node:async_hooks' 278 279 const RequestContextStorage = new AsyncLocalStorage() 280 281 // Define and inject the accessor that next.js will use 282 const RequestContext: NextRequestContext = { 283 get() { 284 return RequestContextStorage.getStore() 285 }, 286 } 287 globalThis[Symbol.for('@next/request-context')] = RequestContext 288 289 const handler = (req, res) => { 290 const contextValue = { waitUntil: YOUR_WAITUNTIL } 291 // Provide the value 292 return RequestContextStorage.run(contextValue, () => nextJsHandler(req, res)) 293 } 294 ``` 295 296
